### Position read
Opening position. Red has advanced from (0,3) to (3,3), occupying the upper-left center. Losses are all zero and every color remains normal.
### Our plan
Build coordinated center pressure with both colors while preserving straight-line mobility. Watch for chances to use same-color distant flanks; avoid friendly-fire sandwiches. Yellow should contest or occupy another center if the opponent does not block it.
### Opponent tendencies
No moves observed yet.
### Lessons
Captures trigger only from the landing square and require the moving color’s own flank. Entering a sandwich is safe. Center occupation wins immediately, so every central vacancy and blocker matters.

### Position read
We occupy (3,3) with Red and now (4,3) with Yellow; Blue occupies (3,4). The final center square (4,4) is empty. All losses remain zero. Yellow at (4,3) blocks Green’s direct row-4 approach from the left to (4,4).
### Our plan
Hold the two central squares and contest (4,4), while seeking a way to dislodge Blue from (3,4). Preserve rook lanes and check every landing for same-color sandwich opportunities and friendly fire.
### Opponent tendencies
The opponent answered our first central advance immediately by placing Blue beside it at (3,4), showing strong center awareness.
### Lessons
Central blockers affect access as much as occupation: placing Yellow at (4,3) prevents the Green piece on row 4 from reaching (4,4) horizontally. Teammate pieces do not form capture flanks.

### Position read
Red can use its piece at (3,3) as the far flank: moving Red from (0,5) to (3,5) captures Blue at (3,4). We retain Red at (3,3) and Yellow at (4,3); center squares (3,4) and (4,4) become empty. Green has advanced to (5,4). Blue now has 1 loss; all others have 0.
### Our plan
Keep our two center occupants, target (3,4) and (4,4), and prevent Green at (5,4) from entering (4,4). Look for another capture on Blue while avoiding teammate lines that could cause friendly fire.
### Opponent tendencies
The opponent contests the center directly and has now developed Green toward the lower central approach after Blue’s occupation was challenged.
### Lessons
A center intruder can be removed efficiently by landing beyond it when an existing same-color center piece supplies the far flank. Always scan lines through occupied center squares before making positional moves.

### Position read
Red occupies (3,3), Yellow occupies (4,3), and Yellow’s move from (7,5) to (4,5) captures Blue at (4,4). Blue should now have 2 losses; all other colors have 0. Green remains advanced at (5,4). Center squares (3,4) and (4,4) are empty.
### Our plan
Blue is one capture from elimination, so prioritize a safe third Blue capture. Preserve our center anchors at (3,3) and (4,3), then occupy (3,4) and (4,4) when tactically secure. Watch Green’s routes from (5,4) into the center.
### Opponent tendencies
The opponent repeatedly inserts Blue directly into central squares and develops Green through the lower-middle approach.
### Lessons
Our center anchors create strong sandwich tactics: a landing just beyond a center intruder can capture it immediately. Recheck teammate pieces in every capture line to avoid friendly fire.

### Position read
We hold (3,3) and (4,3); Green occupies (3,4), with (4,4) empty. Red moved from (0,4) to (2,4), blocking Green’s upward exit while keeping Red anchors at (3,3) and (3,5). Blue has 2 losses and four pieces remaining on the right edge.
### Our plan
Maintain the central net and seek a move-triggered capture of Green; its current side exits are blocked by Red, though it can still move downward. Keep (4,3) secure and prepare occupation of (4,4). Blue is one loss from elimination, so punish any new Blue insertion into a sandwich line.
### Opponent tendencies
The opponent repeatedly inserts Blue into central squares and develops Green into the middle; Green may now retreat from (3,4) through (4,4).
### Lessons
A visually sandwiched piece is not captured without a new landing trigger. Same-color flanks are mandatory, so our mixed-color center control wins by occupation but does not itself enable captures.

### Position read
We occupy (3,3), (4,3), and (4,4); Green remains trapped at (3,4). Yellow’s new (4,4) anchor threatens to capture Blue at (5,4) by moving the Yellow at (7,4) to (6,4), which would give Blue its third loss and eliminate it. Beware Green at (3,0): landing at (3,2) would sandwich our Red at (3,3) against Green at (3,4).
### Our plan
If Blue stays at (5,4), eliminate it with (7,4)->(6,4). Preserve central occupation and seek to replace or protect (3,3) after Green’s likely sandwich. Ultimately remove or induce movement from Green at (3,4) to complete center occupation.
### Opponent tendencies
The opponent inserts Blue into central lanes and uses Green as a central anchor. They now must respond to the Blue-elimination threat and can exploit the Green-flanked Red on row 3.
### Lessons
Enclosure by Yellow cannot remove the trapped Green because adjacent Red pieces join the non-Yellow group and give it liberties. The immediate leverage is the same-color Yellow sandwich threat on Blue.

### Position read
We hold Yellow at (4,3) and (4,4); Green holds (3,2) and (3,4), while (3,3) is empty. Red now stands at (2,3), poised to enter (3,3), with another Red at (3,5). Blue has two losses but can move its threatened piece from (5,4) before Yellow acts.
### Our plan
If (3,3) remains empty, consider Red (2,3)->(3,3); moving into the existing Green sandwich is safe because captures trigger only on the mover’s turn. Preserve the two Yellow center pieces. If Blue remains at (5,4), play Yellow (7,4)->(6,4) to inflict its third loss. Seek a same-color Red flank around Green at (3,4).
### Opponent tendencies
The opponent uses Green to split the upper center and has exploited triggered sandwiches accurately. Expect Blue to evade the threatened Yellow sandwich and Green to contest (3,3).
### Lessons
A piece may safely move into an already sandwiched square. Capturing Green centrally requires same-color flanks; mixed Red and Yellow walls do not form sandwiches.

### Position read
We now hold Yellow at (3,3) and (4,4); Green remains at (3,2) and (3,4). Yellow’s move into the apparent Green sandwich is safe because only a capturing move triggers removal. Red is at (2,3) and (3,5). Blue has two losses and withdrew its vulnerable piece to (5,7).
### Our plan
Protect the central Yellow pieces and refill (4,3), ideally with Yellow from (7,3), if the square remains open. Expect Green at (4,0) to contest (4,3). Look for same-color Red or Yellow flanks against the central Greens; teammate colors cannot complete sandwiches. Continue seeking Blue’s third loss.
### Opponent tendencies
The opponent actively contests central squares and moves threatened pieces away from direct sandwiches. Green may now occupy (4,3) to split our center.
### Lessons
Moving into an already sandwiched position is safe. Center occupation can use both allied colors, but every sandwich requires matching colors at both ends.

### Position read
Yellow holds (3,3) and (4,4), while Green occupies (3,2) and the key center square (3,4). Red has vacated (3,5) to open a direct Yellow route from (7,5). Blue remains one loss from elimination.
### Our plan
If (3,5) stays open, move Yellow from (7,5) to (3,5). That landing sandwiches Green at (3,4) against Yellow at (3,3), clearing the contested center and giving Green its first loss. Then seek occupation of (3,4) and (4,3) to complete the center. Continue watching for Blue’s third loss.
### Opponent tendencies
The opponent contests central squares and may recognize direct sandwich threats. Blue cannot currently reach (3,5) in one rook move, but may create interference or counterplay from column 7.
### Lessons
Same-color geometry can be prepared across turns: clearing a landing square may enable a decisive teammate move, though the teammate still captures only with its own color.

### Position read
Yellow now occupies (3,3), (3,5), and (4,4); the move captures Green at (3,4), giving Green its first loss. Green still presses from (3,2), while Red at (3,6) supports the central corridor. Blue remains one loss from elimination and has advanced to (5,3).
### Our plan
Prioritize filling (3,4) and (4,3) to complete center occupation, while preserving the three current central/near-central pieces. Examine Red’s next turn for a safe move into (3,4) or (4,3), and exploit any available capture to eliminate Blue.
### Opponent tendencies
The opponent contests the center directly and has shifted Blue toward column 3, likely preparing pressure on (4,3) or Yellow’s central structure.
### Lessons
Prepared same-color sandwiches are effective: opening (3,5) let Yellow remove the central blocker immediately.

### Position read
We hold three key central or near-central squares, while the opponent contests the remaining center lanes. Green has one loss, and Blue is one loss from elimination.
### Our plan
Preserve our center pieces and fill (3,4) and (4,3) when legal. Keep pressure on Blue and look for a same-color sandwich that delivers its final loss.
### Opponent tendencies
The opponent contests the center directly and advances pieces into column 3 to disrupt our occupation plan.
### Lessons
Verify the source square against the observed board before submitting. Same-color sandwich preparation remains our strongest tactical tool.

### Position read
We occupy (3,3), (3,4), and (4,4), giving us three of the four central squares. Blue has two losses and is one capture from elimination; Green has no losses. Our Red source at (3,6) moved legally through empty (3,5) to (3,4).
### Our plan
Threaten the center win by moving Yellow from (3,3) to (4,3) if that square remains empty. Expect Blue to occupy (4,3) from (5,3) or otherwise disrupt a central piece. Preserve the central cluster while seeking Blue’s final loss through a Red or Yellow sandwich.
### Opponent tendencies
The opponent directly blocks center-completion threats and uses Green’s column/row mobility to pull pieces away from useful lanes.
### Lessons
Before moving, verify every traversed square and the current color’s source. Center threats are strongest when they force the opponent’s intervening color into a narrow defensive move.

### Position read
We hold three central squares: (3,3), (3,4), and (4,4). Blue has two losses and is one capture from elimination. Red is at (3,6), with (3,5) open; the attempted move to (3,4) failed because that square is occupied.
### Our plan
Keep the central cluster intact and maintain pressure on Blue’s final life. Moving Red to (3,5) improves proximity to the center without disturbing our occupants. On Yellow’s turn, complete the center via (4,3) if it is open; otherwise seek a sandwich that eliminates Blue.
### Opponent tendencies
The opponent blocks immediate center wins and relocates pieces to interfere with central lanes.
### Lessons
Treat occupied friendly central squares as fixed assets. Confirm both the destination and every traversed square before committing.

### Position read
We hold central squares (3,3), (3,4), and (4,4). Yellow’s move from (7,2) to (4,2) sandwiches Blue at (4,3) against Yellow at (4,4), giving Blue its third loss and elimination. Blue’s remaining pieces become Void.
### Our plan
After Blue is eliminated, prioritize occupying (4,3) to complete the four-square center win. Preserve our existing central pieces and keep lanes into (4,3) available. If Green blocks it, use our nearby pieces to dislodge or surround the blocker.
### Opponent tendencies
The opponent recognizes center threats and uses pieces to occupy critical central squares. Expect Green to contest (4,3) immediately if possible.
### Lessons
A teammate does not complete a sandwich flank, but two pieces of the moving color do. Always check direct captures before pursuing center occupation.

### Position read
Blue is eliminated and its three remaining pieces are Void. Green captured our former Yellow center piece at (3,3), but Green at (3,4) was vulnerable between Red’s landing square (3,3) and Red at (3,5). This move captures it. We now occupy center squares (3,3) and (4,4); (3,4) and (4,3) are empty.

### Our plan
On Yellow’s next turn, move Yellow from (4,2) to (4,3) if legal. Green cannot approach (3,4) horizontally through Red at (3,3), so afterward Red should move from (3,5) to (3,4) for immediate center victory. Preserve those pieces and verify any intervening capture.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent used Green to break our center formation immediately. Blue’s Void turns cannot capture but may obstruct lanes; none currently has a direct move to a central square.

### Lessons
Use same-color flank geometry to remove center blockers. After every opponent move, recheck whether the planned center destination was occupied or whether a central piece was captured.

### Position read
Blue is eliminated and its Void move did not affect the center. We now occupy (3,3), (4,3), and (4,4); only (3,4) remains empty. Red at (3,5) has a clear one-step move into it. Green at (3,2) cannot enter (3,4) because Red at (3,3) blocks the lane.

### Our plan
After Green’s intervening turn, recheck all four center squares. If our three center pieces remain and (3,4) is empty, move Red from (3,5) to (3,4) for immediate center victory. If Green disrupts one square, prioritize restoring the center while checking same-color sandwich geometry.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent previously used Green to break center control immediately. Expect Green to attack or obstruct a center piece, although its present lanes do not offer direct access to (3,4).

### Lessons
A three-square center formation is valuable only if the fourth-square move survives the intervening turn. Verify captures and board occupancy before executing the winning move.

### Position read
We occupy three central squares, and Red can legally move from (3,5) into the empty (3,4), completing sole-team occupation of all four center squares.

### Our plan
Complete center occupation now for immediate victory.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent attempted to position Green on (4,6) but could not disrupt the center formation.

### Lessons
When all four center squares can be secured by the acting move, execute immediately; no capture is required for center victory.
